classes.name: Shaman
classes.description:
A campfire collapses into a Shaman's open palm, leaving only cold ash as a fox-shaped ember rises behind them. A stone guardian settles over another Shaman like armor and guides two measured weapon strikes. At the edge of a storm, a third calls a silver hound of lightning that races from enemy to enemy before fading into silence.

Shamans are full spellcasters who form reciprocal bonds with elemental spirits. These spirits temporarily manifest as Embodiments: visible but untargetable magical presences that alter how the Shaman fights, casts, protects allies, heals, or moves. A Shaman remains a capable spellcaster after these spirits fade, but loses the class's strongest and most distinctive abilities until their Spirit Reserve is restored.

- Embodiments -
An Embodiment is not a permanent companion and does not use a creature stat block. It is a temporary expression of a spirit bond: a spectral weapon, guardian animal, elemental warrior, mask, mantle, armor, current, storm, or other manifestation. Different Embodiments require different amounts of Spirit Reserve, and stronger manifestations become available at higher levels.

- Drain -
A Shaman can draw accumulated power from a suitable elemental source. The fire dies, the river stills, the stone cracks, or the storm becomes silent. This Drain can restore Spirit Reserve or help a creature draw on its own vitality, but the source is weakened or consumed. Shamans therefore make practical and moral decisions about what power may safely be taken.

- Creating a Shaman -
When creating a Shaman, consider how the first spirit bond was formed. Did a local spirit choose the character during a disaster? Was the bond inherited through an ancient tradition? Did the Shaman rescue a spirit from corruption, or force it into service? Decide whether the Shaman treats Embodiments as allies, ancestors, tools, fragments of gods, or dangerous beings held under strict ritual control.

In the Monster Hunter campaign, Shamanism can be an ancient predecessor to the modern distinction between Tamers and Absorbers. Tamers develop external creatures, Absorbers internalize conquered essence, and Shamans cooperate with spirits that remain distinct beings even when portions of them manifest through the Shaman.

class_features.feature_detail:
Through reciprocal bonds with elemental spirits, you can cast Shaman spells.

Cantrips.
At 1st level, you know two cantrips of your choice from the Shaman spell list. You learn additional Shaman cantrips at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Shaman table.

Preparing and Casting Spells.
The Shaman table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Shaman spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of Shaman spells available for you to cast, choosing from the Shaman spell list. When you do so, choose a number of Shaman spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your Shaman level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list requires time spent in meditation and communion with your spirits: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

Spellcasting Ability.
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Shaman spells. You use Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Ritual Casting.
You can cast a Shaman spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus.
You can use a druidic focus, carved totem, ritual mask, spirit vessel, sacred stone, or another suitable spiritual implement as a spellcasting focus for your Shaman spells.

The following list is the recommended working Shaman spell list. Spells marked with an asterisk are homebrew spells from Kaatgar's Study Notes or revised spells inspired by that source.

Cantrips
Control Flames, Create Bonfire, Druidcraft, Frostbite, Guidance, Gust, Magic Stone, Mending, Mold Earth, Primordial Bolt*, Produce Flame, Resistance, Shape Water, Shillelagh, Spare the Dying, Thorn Whip, Thunderclap, Word of Ancients*

1st Level
Absorb Elements, Animal Friendship, Charm Person, Create or Destroy Water, Cure Wounds, Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Earth Tremor, Entangle, Faerie Fire, Feather Fall, Fog Cloud, Goodberry, Healing Word, Ice Knife, Jump, Longstrider, Protection from Evil and Good, Purify Food and Drink, Sanctuary, Speak with Animals

2nd Level
Aid, Alter Self, Augury, Beast Sense, Continual Flame, Darkvision, Dust Devil, Enhance Ability, Find Traps, Flame Blade, Gust of Wind, Healing Spirit, Heat Metal, Lesser Restoration, Locate Animals or Plants, Moonbeam, Pass without Trace, Protection from Poison, Skywrite, Spike Growth, Warding Wind

3rd Level
Aura of Vitality, Call Lightning, Clairvoyance, Dispel Magic, Elemental Weapon, Erupting Earth, Gaseous Form, Meld into Stone, Plant Growth, Primordial Guardians*, Protection from Energy, Revivify, Sleet Storm, Speak with Dead, Tidal Wave, Water Breathing, Water Walk, Wind Wall

4th Level
Banishment, Blight, Conjure Minor Elementals, Control Water, Divination, Elemental Bane, Fire Shield, Freedom of Movement, Guardian of Nature, Ice Storm, Locate Creature, Stone Shape, Stoneskin, Storm Sphere, Watery Sphere

5th Level
Commune with Nature, Conjure Elemental, Contact Other Plane, Control Winds, Destructive Wave, Greater Restoration, Maelstrom, Mass Cure Wounds, Planar Binding, Reincarnate, Scrying, Transmute Rock, Wall of Stone

6th Level
Bones of the Earth, Chain Lightning, Find the Path, Heal, Investiture of Flame, Investiture of Ice, Investiture of Stone, Investiture of Storm*, Investiture of Wind, Move Earth, True Seeing

7th Level
Crown of Primordials*, Fire Storm, Plane Shift, Regenerate, Reverse Gravity, Whirlwind

8th Level
Control Weather, Earthquake, Heatburst*, Tsunami

9th Level
Foresight, Mass Heal, Meteor Swarm, Prismatic Wall, Shapechange, Storm of Vengeance

Your bonds can sustain only a limited number of manifestations before their power fades. You have a pool of Spirit Reserve shown in the Shaman table.

You spend Spirit Reserve to manifest Embodiments and fuel certain Shaman features. You regain all expended Spirit Reserve when you finish a long rest. Your Drain feature allows you to recover part of the reserve before a long rest.

You can never have more Spirit Reserve than the maximum shown for your Shaman level.

You can temporarily manifest a bonded elemental spirit. As a bonus action, spend the Embodiment's listed Spirit Reserve cost. The Embodiment manifests for 1 minute.

An Embodiment follows these rules:
 - It is a magical class effect, not a creature or object.
 - It does not occupy a space and cannot be attacked, damaged, grappled, healed, moved, or targeted.
 - It does not require concentration.
 - It is visible or otherwise perceptible unless its description says otherwise.
 - It can appear as a spirit animal, elemental warrior, spectral weapon, mask, mantle, wings, armor, orbiting flame, flowing current, or another form appropriate to the bond.
 - It ends early if you dismiss it, become incapacitated, die, or manifest another Embodiment.
 - It is suppressed inside an antimagic field, though its duration continues to elapse.
 - It cannot normally affect a creature through total cover unless its description says otherwise.

At 1st level, you can maintain only one Embodiment at a time. You do not permanently choose from the general Embodiment list; you can manifest any general Embodiment for which you meet the level and cost requirements. Embodiments granted by a Shamanic Tradition are available only to members of that tradition.

Beginning at 1st level, you can manifest the following Embodiments. Each costs 1 Spirit Reserve.

Embodiment of Protection.
A guardian spirit circles you or hovers behind you. When you or a creature you can see within 10 feet takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by one roll of your Spirit Die. The range becomes 20 feet at 9th level and 30 feet at 17th level.

Embodiment of Focus.
Once on each of your turns, when you cast a Shaman spell using a spell slot, add one roll of your Spirit Die to one damage or healing roll of that spell. A spell affecting multiple creatures gains this bonus only once.

Embodiment of Reach.
A Shaman spell with a range of Touch can originate from an unoccupied point you can see within 30 feet. The spirit can also manipulate unattended objects weighing no more than 10 pounds within 30 feet, but cannot activate magic items or perform tasks requiring fine tool use.

Embodiment of Passage.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet, you ignore nonmagical difficult terrain, and standing from prone costs only 5 feet of movement. Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage during a turn in which you cast a Shaman spell.

Embodiment of Instinct.
You cannot be surprised and have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks. Once during the manifestation, you can add your Spirit Die to an initiative roll or saving throw after seeing the roll but before knowing whether it succeeds.

You learn to draw stored elemental force from an independent source. You perform a 10-minute ritual while touching or remaining immediately beside a suitable source. A source created by you or by one of your spells cannot normally be Drained.

After successfully using Drain, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest. The DM determines a source's strength.

Minor Source.
Examples include a sustained campfire, naturally collected water, a large sun-warmed stone, a powerful natural wind current, or a charged lightning rod. Choose one benefit: recover 1 Spirit Reserve; or one creature immediately spends 1 Hit Die and adds your Wisdom modifier to the healing. The source is extinguished, emptied, cracked, stilled, discharged, or rendered inert.

Potent Source.
Examples include a working forge, flowing stream, large stone formation, violent wind current, active storm front, or elemental engine. Choose one benefit: recover 2 Spirit Reserve; or one creature immediately spends up to 2 Hit Dice and adds your Wisdom modifier to each die. The source is visibly weakened or temporarily disrupted.

Primordial Source.
Examples include a sacred spring, volcanic heart, living mountain shrine, permanent storm, elemental portal, or divine elemental relic. Choose one benefit: recover 3 Spirit Reserve; or one creature immediately spends up to 3 Hit Dice and adds your Wisdom modifier to each die. Draining such a source can have major spiritual, environmental, religious, or political consequences.

Drain is not automatically evil. Its consequences depend on whether the source or its custodian consented, whether the source naturally renews, whether local creatures are harmed, and whether the source is sacred, sentient, unstable, or corrupted.

At 3rd level, choose a Shamanic Tradition from the available traditions. Your choice grants you always-prepared Tradition Spells, tradition-specific Embodiments, and features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, increase two ability scores of your choice by 1, or take a feat if your campaign uses feats. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one cantrip you learned from this class's Spellcasting feature with another cantrip from the Shaman spell list.

You can manifest Embodiments that cost 2 Spirit Reserve. You gain access to the following general Greater Embodiments.

Embodiment of the Spirit Weapon.
When manifested, and as a bonus action on later turns, make a melee spell attack against one creature within 30 feet. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier force damage. The damage becomes 2d8 + your Wisdom modifier at 11th level and 3d8 + your Wisdom modifier at 17th level. The spirit weapon can appear beside any target within range and does not occupy a space.

Embodiment of the Steady Vessel.
You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration. Once during the manifestation, after failing such a save, roll your Spirit Die and add it to the result. You also have advantage on saving throws against possession.

Embodiment of Elemental Shelter.
When manifested, choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder. You have resistance to that damage type. When a creature within 15 feet takes the chosen damage type, you can use a reaction to grant it resistance against that instance of damage. After using this reaction, the Embodiment ends at the end of the current turn.

Embodiment of the Guiding Hand.
When a creature you can see within 30 feet begins its turn, you can use a reaction to let it move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. You can use this reaction a number of times during the manifestation equal to your proficiency bonus.
At 6th level, you gain a feature granted by your Shamanic Tradition.

Your bond becomes harder to disrupt.

- If you become incapacitated, an active Embodiment remains until the end of your next turn rather than ending immediately.
 - You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would sever, suppress, banish, or forcibly disrupt a spirit bond.
 - You can dismiss an Embodiment and manifest another as part of the same bonus action, paying the new Embodiment's full cost.
When you reach 8th level, you gain the Ability Score Improvement feature again.
At 9th level, your Spirit Die becomes a d8.
At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your Shamanic Tradition.

You can manifest Embodiments that cost 3 Spirit Reserve. You gain access to the following general Major Embodiments.

Embodiment of the Primordial Guardian.
You and allies within 10 feet gain half cover against ranged attacks and Dexterity saving throws. Once per round, when a creature in the aura takes damage, reduce that damage by one roll of your Spirit Die without using a reaction. The aura moves with you.

Embodiment of the Great Beast.
When manifested, choose one movement form appropriate to the spirit: a flying speed equal to your walking speed; a swimming speed equal to twice your walking speed and the ability to breathe underwater; a burrow speed of 20 feet through loose earth and sand; or a climbing speed equal to your walking speed and the ability to move across ceilings. You count as one size larger when determining carrying capacity and which creatures you can push, drag, or grapple.

Embodiment of the Second Voice.
Once during the manifestation, when you cast a Shaman spell of 5th level or lower that targets only one creature and does not have a range of Self, you can target a second eligible creature within the spell's range. The second target takes or receives only half of the spell's rolled damage or healing. Other effects occur normally unless the DM determines duplicating them would be inappropriate. After this feature is used, the Embodiment ends at the end of the turn.
When you reach 12th level, you gain the Ability Score Improvement feature again.

Your Drain ritual requires only 1 minute instead of 10 minutes.

When you Drain a Potent or Primordial Source, recover 1 additional Spirit Reserve if you choose Restore Spirit.

After examining a source for 1 minute, you learn whether it is Minor, Potent, or Primordial and whether draining it is likely to awaken, injure, anger, or release a spirit.
At 14th level, you gain a feature granted by your Shamanic Tradition.

You can maintain two Embodiments simultaneously.

- Each Embodiment's full cost must be paid.
 - Each retains its own remaining duration.
 - The same Embodiment cannot be manifested twice.
 - If the same event would trigger features from both Embodiments, only one can apply unless a feature specifically says otherwise.
 - Manifesting a third Embodiment ends one currently active Embodiment of your choice.
When you reach 16th level, you gain the Ability Score Improvement feature again.
At 17th level, your Spirit Die becomes a d10.

When you roll initiative and have no Spirit Reserve remaining, you regain 2 Spirit Reserve.

Once per long rest, when an Embodiment would end because its duration expires, you can extend it for 1 additional minute without paying its cost again.
When you reach 19th level, you gain the Ability Score Improvement feature again.

Your maximum Spirit Reserve becomes 12.

Once on each of your turns, you can manifest a 1-cost Embodiment without spending Spirit Reserve. This free Embodiment lasts until the start of your next turn.

When you use Drain, you can choose both Restore Spirit and Restore Flesh, though the source is affected as if it were one category stronger.

You can communicate with elemental spirits regardless of language.

subclasses.name: Shaman of Fierce Fire
subclasses.description:
Fierce Fire Shamans represent controlled escalation, destruction, passion, purification, hunger, and dangerous renewal.

Their Embodiments improve offensive spellcasting and transform the battlefield into zones of heat and flame. A covenant Shaman treats flame as a living partner; a dominating Shaman consumes every ember until nothing remains but ash.

features.name: Tradition Spells
features.description:
Your bond with spirits of flame grants you additional spells. These spells are always prepared, do not count against the number of spells you can prepare, and count as Shaman spells for you.

Tradition Spells
Shaman Level	Spells
3rd	burning hands, hellish rebuke
5th	flaming sphere, scorching ray
7th	fireball, Ashardalon's stride
9th	fire shield, wall of fire
11th	flame strike, immolation

features.name: Controlled Flame
features.description: When you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier. Chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against that spell and take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Ember Companion
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 1 Spirit Reserve.

A small fire spirit coils around you. Once on each of your turns, when you deal fire damage to a creature, one affected creature takes additional fire damage equal to one roll of your Spirit Die. A creature taking this additional damage cannot benefit from being invisible until the start of your next turn, as flames briefly outline it.

features.name: Living Ember
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 2 Spirit Reserve.

While active, you ignore resistance to fire damage. Once on each turn when you cast a spell that deals fire damage, you can increase one area dimension by 5 feet: radius, cone length, line length, or cube side. You can exclude a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier from the spell's damage. You do not ignore immunity to fire damage.

features.name: Feed the Flame
features.description: When a creature is reduced to 0 hit points by your fire damage, choose one benefit: gain temporary hit points equal to your Shaman level; extend one active Fire Embodiment by 1 round; or move up to half your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Only one creature can trigger this feature per turn.

features.name: Living Inferno
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 3 Spirit Reserve.

A large fire spirit surrounds you. While active, you are immune to fire damage. Hostile creatures that enter a space within 10 feet of you for the first time on a turn or start their turn there take fire damage equal to one roll of your Spirit Die. Fire damage you deal treats immunity as resistance and ignores resistance.

Once during the manifestation, you can cause the spirit to erupt. Each hostile creature within 20 feet makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 6d8 fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The Embodiment then ends.

subclasses.name: Shaman of Enduring Earth
subclasses.description:
Enduring Earth Shamans are armored wardens, immovable guardians, weapon-bearing ritualists, and protectors of settlements, shrines, roads, and mountain passes.

Their martial ability comes from temporary spirit possession rather than permanent fighter-level attack progression.

features.name: Tradition Spells
features.description:
These spells are always prepared, do not count against the number of spells you can prepare, and count as Shaman spells for you.

Tradition Spells
Shaman Level	Spells
3rd	earth tremor, shield
5th	Maximilian's earthen grasp, spike growth
7th	erupting earth, meld into stone
9th	stone shape, stoneskin
11th	transmute rock, wall of stone

features.name: Stone-Bound Training
features.description: You gain proficiency with shields, martial weapons, and heavy armor. After each long rest, choose one weapon with which you are proficient that lacks the heavy property. You can use Wisdom instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls made with that weapon.

features.name: Stoneguard
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 1 Spirit Reserve.

A stone guardian overlaps your body. You have advantage on checks and saving throws made to resist being shoved or knocked prone. When you take bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, you can use a reaction to reduce the damage by one roll of your Spirit Die. If you are standing on natural earth or stone, add your Wisdom modifier to the reduction.

features.name: Stone Warrior
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 2 Spirit Reserve.

A spectral stone warrior guides your weapon. You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action. Once on each of your turns, one weapon hit deals additional damage equal to one roll of your Spirit Die. Your weapon attacks count as magical. This Embodiment does not allow you to cast a cantrip in place of one of the attacks unless another feature says otherwise.

features.name: Rooted Soul
features.description: While touching the ground, you have advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws and cannot be moved against your will unless you choose to be moved. When you succeed on a saving throw against being moved or knocked prone, you can move up to 10 feet toward the source of the effect.

features.name: Earth Colossus
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 3 Spirit Reserve.

A massive earthen spirit encloses you. You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage; your reach with melee weapons increases by 5 feet; and you count as Large if that size would be beneficial. Once on each of your turns, a weapon hit can force the target to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be knocked prone or pushed 10 feet.

You can attack twice whenever you take the Attack action, even if Stone Warrior is not active. If Stone Warrior and Earth Colossus are active simultaneously, you still make only two attacks.

subclasses.name: Shaman of Aggressive Air
subclasses.description:
Aggressive Air Shamans are mobile spell-blades, scouts, duelists, messengers, and hunters who strike before an enemy can establish control.

Their Extra Attack is a temporary spirit-guided combat mode, while their permanent features emphasize movement, projectile defense, and control of position.

features.name: Tradition Spells
features.description:
These spells are always prepared, do not count against the number of spells you can prepare, and count as Shaman spells for you.

Tradition Spells
Shaman Level	Spells
3rd	feather fall, zephyr strike
5th	gust of wind, warding wind
7th	fly, wind wall
9th	freedom of movement, storm sphere
11th	control winds, steel wind strike

features.name: Windblade Training
features.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons that lack the heavy property. You can use Wisdom instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls made with finesse weapons.

features.name: Whispering Current
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 1 Spirit Reserve.

A thin current of visible air circles you. Your walking speed increases by 10 feet. After you cast a Shaman spell, you can move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. You can move through the space of a hostile creature one size larger than you, though that space is difficult terrain.

features.name: Gale Duelist
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 2 Spirit Reserve.

A translucent warrior of compressed wind mirrors your attacks. You can attack twice whenever you take the Attack action. After making a weapon attack, hit or miss, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. Once on each of your turns, a weapon hit can push the target 5 feet.

features.name: Deflecting Current
features.description: When you or a creature within 15 feet is hit by a ranged weapon attack, you can use your reaction and roll your Spirit Die. Reduce the attack's damage by the result + your Wisdom modifier. If this reduces the damage to 0, you can redirect the projectile toward another creature within 30 feet of the original target. Make a ranged spell attack; on a hit, the new target takes the weapon's normal damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses after a long rest.

features.name: Tempest Wings
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 3 Spirit Reserve.

Large wings, ribbons, or a predatory air spirit manifest around you. You gain a flying speed of 60 feet and can hover. Opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage. Once on each of your turns, after dealing damage, you can move up to 15 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. When you deal damage to a creature, you can move it 10 feet in any horizontal direction if it fails a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC.

subclasses.name: Shaman of Wild Water
subclasses.description:
Wild Water Shamans manipulate the distribution of vitality, movement, poison, pressure, and harm.

They are healers and protectors, but their healing is intended to remain less efficient than that of a dedicated Cleric unless they also spend Spirit Reserve.

features.name: Tradition Spells
features.description:
These spells are always prepared, do not count against the number of spells you can prepare, and count as Shaman spells for you.

Tradition Spells
Shaman Level	Spells
3rd	create or destroy water, cure wounds
5th	healing spirit, lesser restoration
7th	tidal wave, water breathing
9th	control water, watery sphere
11th	greater restoration, maelstrom

features.name: Flowing Mercy
features.description: Once on each of your turns, when you restore hit points to a creature using a spell, choose one benefit for that creature: it moves 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks; it gains temporary hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier; or it can immediately stand from prone without spending movement.

features.name: River Keeper
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 1 Spirit Reserve.

A water spirit circles you and nearby allies. Once on each of your turns, when you restore hit points to one creature, a second creature within 15 feet of the first regains hit points equal to one roll of your Spirit Die. The same creature cannot receive both the original healing and River Keeper healing from the same spell.

features.name: Current Bearer
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 2 Spirit Reserve.

When an ally within 30 feet is targeted by an attack, you can use a reaction to move that ally up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. If the movement places the ally outside the attacker's reach or range, the attack misses. Once on each of your turns, when a spell restores hit points, you can transfer up to one roll of your Spirit Die of that healing from the original target to another creature within 30 feet.

features.name: Purifying Current
features.description: When you restore hit points to a creature using a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also end one of the following on that creature: the poisoned, blinded, or deafened condition; one disease; or one nonmagical toxin or contamination. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier, regaining all uses after a long rest. After expending those uses, you can spend 1 Spirit Reserve to use it again.

features.name: Deep Current
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 3 Spirit Reserve.

A large current surrounds you in a 15-foot aura. You and allies in the aura have resistance to acid and cold damage. Once per round, when an ally in the aura takes damage, you can redirect damage equal to one roll of your Spirit Die to yourself; this redirected damage cannot be reduced. At the start of each of your turns, choose one creature in the aura; it regains hit points equal to your Wisdom modifier.

Once during the manifestation, you can release a restorative wave. Chosen creatures in the aura regain 4d8 + your Wisdom modifier hit points, and the Embodiment ends.

subclasses.name: Shaman of Loose Lightning
subclasses.description:
Loose Lightning Shamans bond with volatile storm spirits and specialize in priority targets, chain effects, sudden repositioning, and marking enemies as conductors.

Lightning Genasi possess lightning innately. A Lightning Shaman negotiates with and directs a separate lightning spirit. A Lightning Genasi can become a Lightning Shaman, but the two concepts are not interchangeable.

features.name: Tradition Spells
features.description:
These spells are always prepared, do not count against the number of spells you can prepare, and count as Shaman spells for you. Lightning Discharge and Storm Strike are homebrew spells requiring final revision.

Tradition Spells
Shaman Level	Spells
3rd	thunderwave, witch bolt
5th	misty step, shatter
7th	lightning bolt, thunder step
9th	lightning discharge, storm sphere
11th	destructive wave, storm strike

features.name: Conductor Mark
features.description: Once on each of your turns, when you deal lightning or thunder damage to a creature, you can mark it until the start of your next turn. The next attack roll made against the marked creature before the mark ends gains a bonus equal to one roll of your Spirit Die. Only one creature can be marked at a time.

features.name: Storm Hound
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 1 Spirit Reserve.

A small lightning beast races between targets. Once on each of your turns, when you deal lightning or thunder damage to a creature, choose a second creature within 10 feet of it. The second creature takes lightning damage equal to one roll of your Spirit Die.

features.name: Flash Spirit
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 2 Spirit Reserve.

When you are targeted by an attack, you can use a reaction to teleport up to 15 feet to a space you can see. If the teleport moves you outside the attack's reach or range, the attack misses. Once on each of your turns, after dealing lightning or thunder damage, you can teleport 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

features.name: Living Conduit
features.description: You gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. When you succeed on a saving throw against lightning or thunder damage, you can cause one creature within 30 feet to take lightning damage equal to one roll of your Spirit Die. You can do this once per round.

features.name: Thunder Twin
features.description:
Embodiment; Cost 3 Spirit Reserve.

Once on each of your turns, when a Shaman spell deals lightning or thunder damage to exactly one creature, a second eligible creature within 30 feet of the first takes lightning or thunder damage equal to half the damage dealt to the first creature. You can use a reaction to teleport 30 feet when a creature affected by your lightning or thunder damage moves.

Once during the manifestation, you can cast a lightning or thunder spell of 5th level or lower that normally targets one creature and target two creatures instead. The Embodiment then ends.
